title: An official at Peking to an unnamed addressee, October 1912: the telegram on the restoration of the Dalai Lama's title that the Government of India 'could not properly decypher' (lead 2465, NAI Deposit Cypher 1912 Nos. 86-87): plain Chinese standard telegraph code read by rows, 30 of 31 codes read with the public table (an approximate English translation was made by the General Staff in 1912)

documents.shelfmark: National Archives of India, Foreign Department, Deposit Cypher, 1912, Nos. 86-87, p. 6 (Abhilekh Patal PR_000004118254; duplicate record PR_000006222155)
documents.route: Peking (an official; the record title has 'Yaoshikinan, Peking', and the telegram names the President in the third person) to an unnamed Chinese addressee reached over the Indian lines (a duplicate came through Kalimpong); intercepted and copied by the Government of India

plaintext.source: An approximate English translation by the General Staff, Simla, sent by Col. A. H. Bingley on 8 Oct 1912, in the same file (p. 9), with two alternative readings (A, B); no Chinese text.

transcription.source: Abhilekh Patal online reader, screen captures (images not reproduced)
transcription.notes: Claude Opus 5.5 agent, 11 Nov 2026: 25 groups of five digits in four columns (7, 6, 6, 6); every digit clear. Not checked against the image by anyone but the contributor: Abhilekh Patal shows a human check to scripts, and the pull request carries no image (integration, 12 Nov 2026).

system.summary: Plain Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit codes), with no encipherment. The 125 digits were written in groups of five, so the four-digit codes run across group boundaries; the groups must be read by rows (four per row), not down the columns as laid out on the copy. 31 codes + 1 filler digit.
system.notes: The last digit (0 of 60100) is a filler. The Foreign Department's failure (record title 'which cannot be properly decyphered') is explained by the regrouping in fives and the column layout of the copy, not by any secret key. The methods found in NAI Foreign Dept. 1907 File 45506 (Campbell's 'transparency' key, the General Staff's column formula, Webster's dictionary, a 5-digit code) were prepared as hypotheses but were not needed.

prior_solution.where: General Staff, Simla, 8 Oct 1912: approximate English translation with two alternative readings, in the same file (p. 9); Chinese text not given. Lead 2465 (Daniel Bourdeau, research/leads.json): open as checked 11 Nov 2026; web search 11 Nov 2026: nothing printed; one more web search on the Chinese phrases at verification (12 Nov 2026): nothing. Chinese printed document collections were not searched.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target, logged in to Abhilekh Patal and captured the pages, and set the rules (protocol written and hashed before the attack; every decipherment goes to Daniel). Integration (12 Nov 2026): the decoding and the controls were re-run for the project with an independent decoder and Unihan table; the images were not seen (the archive shows a human check to scripts).
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout (protocol, reading, controls, write-up)

solution.what: File seen after login on Abhilekh Patal (PR_000004118254), pp. 3-13; the groups (p. 6) and the General Staff translation (p. 9) captured; no PDF (download not offered).
Lead 2465 status (open), web search: no publication of the telegram or its Chinese text.

Protocol hashed before the attack, by the contributor's record (frozen/PREREG.md, SHA-256 46310551...): H0 plain standard telegraph code in four reading orders and cuts; H1-H4 additives (5- and 4-digit), Campbell's 'transparency' relation, the General Staff's column formula. H0 by rows worked at once: 電悉大總統...; H1-H4 not needed.

Crib score (words fixed in the protocol from the 1912 translation): by rows 19; by columns 0; 1,000 random orders of the 25 groups max 6 (mean 1.22); 1,000 random 4-digit additives max 1 (frozen/controles.out). Both halves read independently (14 and 5).
31 codes, 31 characters; 30 give the character as written, 1 emended (1770 徇, read 1769 待) and not counted as read.

Integration of PR #431 after an independent verification: a separate decoder with a code table built from Unihan.zip (same SHA-256) gives 31 codes + 1 filler digit, 31 of 31 matching decryption.txt; frozen/controles.py rerun gives controles.out byte for byte (rows 19, columns 0, random orders max 6, additives max 1, halves 14 and 5); row offsets 1-3, columns at four offsets and drop-one-digit cuts give gibberish; of the 36 one-digit neighbours of 1770 only 1769 待 gives a word with 優. PREREG hash matches. Corrections: class 'already solved' -> 'read' (as targets/ctcplain1913), provenance 'mixed' -> 'contributed', the 1770 gap is an emendation not an illegible sign, 是否通過 left ambiguous in the translation, sender is an official (the President is in the third person), not Yuan Shikai. Not done: no image was seen (Abhilekh Patal shows a human check to scripts; not gone round).

outcome.method_basis: The key is the public Chinese standard telegraph code (table from Unicode Unihan, kTaiwanTelegraph / kMainlandTelegraph); what had to be found was the reading order (rows) and the cut into four-digit codes across the five-digit groups. No Chinese text existed: the General Staff's file of 1912 holds an approximate English translation only.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 30 of 31 codes give the character as written and read as sense; 1 emended (code 1770 徇, read 1769 待) and not counted, by the read bar; recounted at integration.

texts.label: Peking telegram, received at Simla by 3 Oct 1912 (NAI Deposit Cypher 1912, Nos. 86-87, p. 6)
texts.summary: Telegram received. The President has long since approved restoring the Dalai Lama's title and allows him to come to the capital, where he will be specially welcomed and generously treated (優待 by emendation of one code). Reply quickly whether it has passed (是否通過, ambiguous). The General Staff's reading A of 1912 (restoration of the title) is confirmed.

reading_review.by: integration review for the project (independent verification, then the integrator)
reading_review.note: Read as one sentence group of telegraphic Chinese: 電悉 opening, 大總統早經允准復回達賴名號，並允到京，格外歡迎優待, closing 是否通過，速覆. Coherent from end to end; one emended code (1770 徇 for 1769 待); 是否通過 is ambiguous. First read by the contributor's agent on 11 Nov 2026. No sinologist has re-read it, and the transcription was not checked against the image.

outcome.notes: No image of the NAI file is included (Abhilekh Patal images, no reuse licence shown; the site shows a human check to scripts). Not a first break: the General Staff translated the telegram approximately in 1912. What is new here is the Chinese text, the way the copy must be read, and the choice between the General Staff's readings A and B. outcome.key is 'not applicable', as in targets/ctcplain1913: the key is a public table and nothing was recovered.
